options: A detailed record of only cash transactions
The master record of all of a business's accounts and their balances
A list of all supplier invoices only
A report generated only once a year
questions.explain: The general ledger is the master record of every account (assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses) and its balance.

questions.q: Why do businesses use subledgers instead of recording every individual transaction directly in the general ledger?
options: Because subledgers are legally required for tax purposes
Because the general ledger cannot technically hold any transactions
Because subledgers replace the need for a general ledger entirely
Because posting enormous volumes of individual detail directly into the main ledger would bury the big picture in overwhelming detail
questions.explain: Subledgers track detailed, process-specific transactions and periodically summarize into the GL, keeping the main ledger at a manageable, meaningful level of detail.

questions.q: What happens to detailed subledger transactions once they are summarized into the general ledger?
options: They still exist in the subledger, and a well-designed system allows drilling down from the GL balance back to them
They are permanently deleted and cannot be viewed again
They are converted into a completely different account type
They are moved out of the accounting system entirely
questions.explain: The underlying detail is preserved in the subledger; drilling down from a GL balance to the originating transactions is a key feature of a well-designed system.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a subledger in Oracle Fusion Financials?
options: General Ledger itself
The chart of accounts
Accounts Payable
The accounting equation
questions.explain: Accounts Payable (along with Receivables and Fixed Assets) is a subledger that tracks detailed, process-specific transactions before summarizing into the GL.

questions.q: What role does Oracle Fusion's Subledger Accounting (SLA) engine play in this architecture?
options: It replaces the general ledger entirely
It applies configurable accounting rules to transform subledger transaction detail into correctly formed, summarized GL journal entries
It only tracks customer names and addresses
It has no connection to journal entries
questions.explain: Subledger Accounting sits between the subledgers and the General Ledger, turning detailed transactions into properly structured summarized journal entries.
